paras: The killing of Joshua Anderson was the fatal stabbing of a farmer near Owensboro, Kentucky, in late spring 1888 by one of four men who had disguised themselves as "White Caps" to whip him. The men were said to have whipped Anderson once and ordered him to leave, then killed him when they tried to whip him a second time; the principals were arrested.

Anderson was described as "a quiet farmer living near Owensboro, Ky.", and no race was given for him or for the men who attacked him. The report named the attackers as Buck and Jerry Rasher, John Burns and James Holderman.

Disguised as "White Caps", the four men took Anderson out, "thrashed" him, and ordered him to leave the area. When he did not leave, he was "enticed" to the vicinity of Holderman's house, where, according to the report, arrangements had been made to whip him again. Anderson resisted and struck one of the men, and Buck Rasher then seized a knife and, in the paper's words, "cut Anderson's heart out." The report gave no date beyond "a few days ago" and did not say how long passed between the two encounters.
"The principals in the affair have been arrested," the report stated, without naming which of the four were held. No report of an inquest, indictment or trial appears in the coverage.

The only account found ran on 15 June 1888 in the West Tennessee Star of Bolivar, Tennessee, as one paragraph in its "Southern Gleanings" column of regional news. The item called the killing "the outrage" and the planned whipping "this brutality", and it stated that "there was no particular cause" for the attack. It cited no local paper or dispatch, and no Kentucky report of the killing appears in the coverage.

Four men acting together in a disguised White Cap whipping killed Anderson without legal authority, one of them using a knife (A1); the brief gives 'no particular cause', so the pretext rests only on the White Cap disguise and the order to leave (A1).
The only report found is one unsourced brief in a Tennessee weekly's roundup of Southern news (A1).
